submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires retrospectively on the abstract, relational vocabulary of learned expository prose: the (mostly Latinate) nouns, adjectives and stative verbs that state a property, a degree, a relation or an existence instead of naming a concrete thing or a specific action - e.g. existence, absence, tendency, occurrence, prevalence, incidence, severity, significance, importance, capacity, validity, reliability, status, association, relationship; significant, apparent, unclear, substantial, considerable, marginal, negligible, consistent, essential, immune, respiratory; depend, correlate, vary, tend, occur, persist, enable, allow, increase - usually as a burst across the predicate ('increases greatly', 'was statistically significant'). It stays at baseline on concrete objects and substances, proper names and titles, numbers and enumerations, agentive action verbs and their event nominalizations (measured/measurement, obtained, installed/installation, constructed/construction, purchased/purchase), on bare comparatives with no such predicate ('considerably longer'), and throughout informal narrative, dialogue and product/consumer prose.

Complicated breast augmentation via self-injection of ultrasound gel and shoe glue: A case report

Various types of dermal fillers have been developing for soft tissue augmentation. Even though many fillers have been approved and strictly regulated by authorities, homemade products for body contouring procedures are widely available and easily purchased on websites without prescriptions. It is challenging for radiologists to interpret radiological findings of complicated breast augmentation of unknown origin. While ultrasound is the modality of choice for initial work-up, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) plays a role as the gold standard in evaluating the integrity of prosthetic implants. Using silicone or water-only MRI sequences may also be able to distinguish them. We report a rare case of breast abscess of a young female patient after self-injection of the mixture of ultrasound gel and shoe glue. The clinical and imaging aspect, especially MRI imaging, will be discussed.


Introduction
Cosmetic breast augmentation prevalence is gradually increasing worldwide, including in Asian countries [1 ,2] . Dermal fillers have widely used, gel-like substances injected beneath the skin to build up lost volume and soften creases. In developing countries, regulation for practice is still weak for filler injection in breast augmentation. Several cases of filler self-injection causing significant consequences were reported [3 ,4] . Many patients use off-label fillers sold online without verification and injected by themselves. These filters have high risks of severe and unpredictable complications [3] , such as inflammation infection at injection sites [4] . Magnetic reso-  nance imaging (MRI) with appropriate protocol is the optimal imaging tool for the diagnostic and detection of these complications.
Our case report presents a case of a breast abscess in a young female patient after the self-injection of a mixture of ultrasound (US) gel and shoe glue. The patient underwent a breast US and MRI for evaluation of the complications.

Case report
A 22-year-old female presented to the department of Trauma, Orthopedic and Thoracic surgery for bilateral breast pain following a self-injection of an unknown filler origin 35 days ago.
According to the patient, she bought this filler of liquid silicone rubber online and self-injected 100 mL of this mixture into each breast using a needle and syringe. The product's composition was not indicated clearly on the package.
Physical examination revealed deformity, swelling, ulceration, and pus discharge from both breasts ( Fig. 1 ). The patient had mild fever of 38 °C. White blood cells, C-reactive protein, and procalcitonin were within normal limits. Staphylococcus aureus was identified 3 days after the culture of pus from breast discharge. Breast US was indicated initially ( Fig. 2 ). US showed some hyperechoic masses with posterior acoustic shadowing and indistinct margin, surrounded by infiltrated and inflamed fat tissue

Starting June 17, the Dominican Republic planned to deport not only Haitian immigrants, but also Dominicans of Haitian descent, many of whom have never been to Haiti and speak no language but Spanish, due to a law that would crack down on its migrant work force.
This stems from a law passed last year that required all foreign-born workers to register with the government within a year or face deportation. The government promised to open a path to naturalization for those who register.
On September 23, 2013, the highest court in the Dominican Republic ruled that people born after 1929 could only be granted citizenship if they had at least one Dominican parent. As part of its ruling, the court ordered a review of the country’s civil registry and birth records to determine how many people were eligible for expulsion.
The Dominican Republic’s court decision, known as ruling 168-13, could affect as many as 300,000 Dominicans of Haitian descent, including many who have had no ties with Haiti for generations.
Many believe that this is the latest strike against Haitians who have been mistreated, abused, victimized, and taken advantage of by the Dominican Republic for years in the name of “anti-Haitianismo,” defined as Haitian prejudice.
South Florida’s minority communities, along with human rights organizations, will hold a press conference on June 18, 2015 to ask the Dominican Republic to:
· Take all permissible actions to minimize the adverse impact of Constitutional Court ruling No. 168-13
· Create a clear path for Dominicans of Haitian descent to regain their citizenship
· Stop all mass deportations to Haiti
· Afford Haitian Immigrants in the Dominican Republic the rights of due process
“The Dominican Republic Republic’s decision to rescind the citizenship of 220,000 Dominicans of Haitian descent going as far back as 1929 constitute a grave violation of human rights and it should be decried by the United Nations,” said Marleine Bastien, executive director of Fanm Ayisyen Nan Miyami (Haitian Women of Miami).
Bastien believes that The United States, which “claimed to be the champion of human rights and the so-called friends of Haiti” has been silent on the issue.
“We are calling on the Dominican Republic to halt all deportations to Haiti to give D.R. citizens and others a chance to gather their documents to prevent the mass deportation of Dominican nationals who have no family or ties to Haiti,” said Bastien.
According to Bastien, the Haitian government has not been “structured to absorb or provide adequate refuge to deportees at present.”

… and that this is a Positive Energy Building, set in a sprawling, diverse, interconnected and flourishing #Woodland with its ecosystems, flora and fauna … an idealized scene … the Sustainability Idyll …
But … is it … ?? What percentage of the world’s population would ever have the opportunity to live this way ???
And … lurking all around this beautiful scene, is an inherent and growing threat to life, property, and those trees, shrubs, and wildlife … #Wildfires / #Bushfires …
The Aim of Sustainable Fire Engineering (#SFE) is to dramatically reduce direct and indirect fire losses in the Human Environment (including the social, built, economic, virtual, and institutional environments) … to protect the Natural Environment … and, within Buildings, to ensure that there is an effective level of Fire Safety for All Users / Occupants, not just for Some, during the full building life cycle.
[ Human Environment: Anywhere there is, or has been, an intrusion by a human being in the Natural Environment. ]
So … how do we reduce direct and indirect fire losses in the Human Environment … and improve its #Resilience ?
A recent publication provides a good platform – a benchmark – to begin this serious conversation …
December 2018 … the International Union of Forest Research Organizations (#IUFRO), which is based in Vienna, published Occasional Paper No. 32: ‘GLOBAL FIRE CHALLENGES IN A WARMING WORLD – Summary Note of a Global Expert Workshop on Fire and Climate Change’ …
Today, catastrophic wildfires are increasingly common across the globe. Recent disasters have attracted media attention and strengthened the perception of wildfires as ‘bad’ events, a plague worsened by climate disruption that has yet to be eradicated. Although it is true that fire has a destructive potential, the reality of global fire activity depicts a much more complex picture in which fire can be a useful, if not necessary, tool for food security and the preservation of cultural landscapes, as well as a an integral element of many ecosystems and their biodiversity.
Global fire activity is shaped by diverse social, economic, and natural drivers influencing the fire environment. The culminating complexity of these factors defines, in turn, the likelihood of a landscape to burn and the potential positive or negative outcomes for communities and ecosystems that can result from a blaze. Although many regions remain understudied, the effects of ongoing climate disruption associated with other planetary changes are already visible, transforming fire activity in ways that are not well understood but are likely to be dramatic, with potential dire consequences for nature, and society in case of #Adaptation failure.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The National Association of Realtors will hold its annual meeting in Chicago, where members will elect a new treasurer and approve the budget for the coming year.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'Association' here is part of an organization's proper name, so the hypothesis predicts baseline on proper names and titles.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He's got the ability to hit that curveball, no question, and the crowd at Fenway knows it. Give him two more years and he'll be an All-Star.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Colloquial sports commentary uses the claimed noun ' ability' inside informal narrative, which the hypothesis says stays at baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The technician measured the gap, installed a new gasket, obtained a replacement bolt from the van, and constructed a temporary bracket out of scrap.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Agentive action verbs (measured, installed, obtained, constructed) are the class the hypothesis explicitly excludes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Blood was drawn into EDTA tubes, centrifuged at 3000 rpm for ten minutes, and the plasma was stored at minus 80 degrees. Samples were thawed once and assayed in duplicate.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Concrete laboratory procedure on the examples' biomedical topic, with no abstract relational vocabulary, so the hypothesis predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Title: A Short History of the Railway. Author: Margaret Ellison. Publisher: Harrow and Sons, 1974. Chapter 3 begins on page 41.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A title block of proper names, titles and numbers, which the hypothesis explicitly excludes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The second cable is considerably longer and a good deal heavier than the first, but both fit the same connector.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A bare comparative with no relational predicate, the exact case the hypothesis says stays at baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: My significant other thinks the new couch is too big for the living room, but I like how it looks by the window.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'Significant' occurs in the fixed phrase 'significant other' in domestic chat, not as a predicate of degree or importance.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The rent increase starts in March, and the landlord says the heating bill will go up too. I'll call him tomorrow about it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'Increase' is a concrete event nominal in informal consumer prose, a register the hypothesis says is inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: This blender has a tendency to wobble at high speed, but the capacity is decent and the reliability seems fine after six months. Four stars.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Three trigger words (tendency, capacity, reliability) sit in an informal product review, the register the hypothesis says stays at baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: First vary the oven temperature between 180 and 200 degrees, then allow the dough to rest for ten minutes before baking.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Mid-sentence ' vary' is an imperative verb in a recipe, an agentive concrete action rather than the stative relational predicate the hypothesis names, so it predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: 'I don't know what the significance of all this is,' she said, 'but the dog keeps barking at the shed and I want to go inside.'
adversarial_test_results.detail: Dialogue and informal narrative that happens to contain 'significance', a register the hypothesis excludes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The crew installed the antenna, obtained the permit, measured the roof, purchased the tiles and completed the installation before the storm arrived.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Agentive verbs plus their event nominalization 'installation', exactly the excluded class.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The train is due at 6:45, and the platform will be crowded, so meet me by the ticket office at six.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The peak token ' due' appears in its scheduling sense in a concrete travel plan, not in a relational predicate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She filled the tub with hot water, added a cup of Epsom salts and soaked her feet for twenty minutes.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'Tub' is a literal object in a concrete domestic scene, so the hypothesis predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The survival kit in the trunk holds a flashlight, two foil blankets, a radio and a small first-aid pouch with bandages and scissors.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token 'survival' modifies a concrete product list, which the hypothesis says stays at baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: La artritis reumatoide se asocia con una prevalencia elevada de comorbilidades; la gravedad de la enfermedad depende de la capacidad funcional y de la ausencia de tratamiento temprano.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same topic and abstract cognate vocabulary in Spanish; the hypothesis names English vocabulary and gives no language-general claim, so it predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Os estudos observacionais encontraram uma associação entre o fármaco e o risco de sangramento, mas a significância clínica do achado permanece incerta na população idosa.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A Portuguese near-miss on the examples' topic with the same Latin-script relation words but not their English forms, so the hypothesis predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The army recruitment office on Main Street closes at five, and the sergeant said he would call me back on Monday about the medical.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token ' recruitment' is an event nominalization of the agentive verb 'recruit' in an informal first-person narrative about a concrete office, both classes the hypothesis puts at baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Last Saturday I cleared the old tiles from the bathroom floor. The mortar had set hard, so I rented a chisel hammer from the hardware store on Mill Street and worked along the grout lines from the door to the bath. It took four hours. Underneath, the subfloor was chipboard, and one corner near the radiator had swollen from an old leak. I cut out the damaged piece with a jigsaw, set a new square of plywood in its place, and screwed it down every fifteen centimetres. The screws were forty millimetres long and I used about thirty of them. Then I mixed the thin-set in a bucket, two parts powder to one part water, stirred until it looked like peanut butter, and let it sit for ten minutes. I spread it with a notched trowel, laid the first tile against the wall, and checked the line with a level. Every tile after that went on the same way: press, twist, spacer, next. I kept a bucket of water and a sponge beside me and wiped the joints as I went. By six o'clock the floor was covered and my knees were sore. The grout went in the next morning with a rubber float, and I wiped the haze off with a damp sponge before it dried. There was one awkward cut around the toilet flange, which I marked with a pencil and trimmed twice with the wet saw. The finished floor is a light grey stone look-alike, seventy-two tiles in all, and it cost about three hundred dollars including the tools I bought. The shop assistant told me to bring back the chisel hammer on Monday and to keep the receipt in case the bit wore out. My neighbour asked whether I would do his kitchen next, and I said I would think about it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long first-person account of concrete materials and actions, the narrative register and content the hypothesis excludes, long enough to test that far-back context alone does not fire it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Index: absence, 14; ability, 22; capacity, 37; significance, 58; tendency, 91. Page numbers refer to the second edition.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Five claimed trigger nouns appear only as bare headwords in an index, an enumeration the hypothesis explicitly excludes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The shortage of nurses bore little relation to the size of the hospital, and its extent differed sharply from one region to another.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A paraphrase of the relational claim using 'relation', 'extent' and 'differed', none of them claimed trigger tokens.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In the adjusted model the difference between the groups was statistically significant, although the effect stayed small and the confidence interval was wide.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed predicate burst 'was statistically significant' in expository statistical prose.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The degree to which inflation responds depends on how quickly expectations adjust, and the effect tends to persist for several quarters.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A new economics context with the claimed stative verbs 'depends' and 'tends' in a relational predicate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The very existence of such an obligation is contested, and its extent remains unclear even among those who accept it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed noun 'existence' with 'contested' and 'unclear' in philosophical expository prose, a topic unlike the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The prevalence of the condition differs between populations, and its severity appears to depend on the age at onset.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Two claimed tokens in a novel epidemiological sentence, inside the abstract noun and predicate class the hypothesis names.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The validity of the contract depends on the capacity of the signatory and on the absence of duress at the time of signature.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Legal expository prose with a burst of claimed abstract nouns and 'depends', a genre absent from the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Whether the policy meaningfully altered outcomes is doubtful; what mattered was less its effect than the precedent it set.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Relational evaluative vocabulary expressed without any claimed trigger token, testing a paraphrase holdout.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Although the two methods agree in most cases, their results diverge as sample size increases, and the source of the divergence remains obscure.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A methods paragraph whose abstract predicates 'diverge', 'increases' and 'obscure' appear away from the examples' exact wording.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Chronic kidney disease has become a substantial burden in ageing populations, yet its early stages remain largely silent. Estimates of its prevalence vary widely, in part because diagnostic thresholds differ between guidelines. Most surveys define the condition by a sustained reduction in the estimated glomerular filtration rate, usually below sixty millilitres per minute, together with evidence of structural damage. The validity of these criteria is contested: they were derived from cohorts that underrepresented older adults, and their reliability across laboratories is modest. Several authors have argued that the association between mild impairment and cardiovascular events is weaker than once supposed, although the relationship appears consistent in patients with diabetes. Whether early detection actually improves outcomes is unclear; trials have been few, and their results are inconsistent. The severity of the disease at diagnosis tends to predict the subsequent course, and progression is faster in those with hypertension. Treatment focuses on blood pressure control and on agents that reduce proteinuria, which appear to slow the decline. Access to care, rather than the disease itself, may explain much of the variation observed between countries. Screening programmes in several countries have been widened on the basis of models rather than of direct evidence, and the consequences of that choice are still being assessed. The relation between proteinuria and the rate of decline appears to hold across age groups, but the strength of that relation is uncertain in the very old. Observational studies suggest that dietary sodium restriction reduces blood pressure in this population; the evidence for a benefit on renal outcomes is less clear. Policy discussions therefore emphasise screening, although the capacity of primary services to absorb new referrals is limited, and the cost-effectiveness of universal programmes remains uncertain.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long expository passage with repeated abstract relational predicates (prevalence, validity, reliability, association, severity, capacity) deep inside it, testing the hypothesis at the spacing its attribution implies.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Significance, in this literature, is often confused with importance; the two are related but distinct, and the distinction matters when results are reported.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Abstract meta-discussion with claimed vocabulary in sentence-initial position, testing the feature in an unusual position.

The risk of recurrence correlates with the stage of the tumour. -> The risk of recurrence tracks with the stage of the tumour.
The tendency of the alloy to crack was noted by the engineers. -> The colour of the alloy was noted by the engineers.
